channel.title: Finality
channel.description: Finality reports crypto news: protocol upgrades, network incidents, exchange and stablecoin developments, regulation and the projects shaping blockchain.

item.title: Cross-chain swap rates are route prices, not token prices
item.description: Cross-chain swap rates depend on executable output after price impact, bridge fees, gas, settlement time, and failure risk; compare the full route, not its headline quote.

item.title: Check the destination before sending through a crypto bridge
item.description: A bridge transfer can settle on the wrong chain or into the wrong asset contract; verify the destination network, token representation, route and recipient first.

item.title: Circle plans entry into about 40 emerging markets
item.description: Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire says the issuer will pursue about 40 emerging markets as rising stablecoin demand pushes USDC toward mainstream use globally.

item.title: Exchange Maintenance Can Hold a Treasury Withdrawal Before Broadcast
item.description: Exchange maintenance can stop a treasury withdrawal before it reaches a blockchain. The transaction’s status shows whether the delay sits with the venue or network.

item.title: Should You Approve a Mantle Bridge Prompt Twice?
item.description: A repeated Mantle bridge approval signs an ERC-20 allowance change, not a second transfer; check the spender, amount and pending transaction before signing.

item.title: Hardware Wallets Can Sign Mantle Bridge Transactions
item.description: A hardware wallet can authorize Mantle bridge calls through an EVM wallet interface, but deposits, token approvals and Ethereum claims may each need separate signatures.

item.title: Recurring Treasury Transfers Need a Recovery Path
item.description: Recurring treasury transfers are safest when execution, recipient checks and token recovery sit in a narrowly scoped contract with explicit roles and limits.

item.title: Why Cross-Chain Route Types Change Your Minimum
item.description: A cross-chain minimum depends on where swaps run: before the bridge, after it, or on both sides, and which leg enforces minimum output for the final token.

item.title: How to Make Cross-Chain Payroll Transfers on Time
item.description: Payroll deadlines depend on destination-chain settlement, not the moment a bridge transaction is submitted; plan around finality, liquidity, and payout execution.

item.title: Retry a Cross-Chain Swap Only After Its First Route Resolves
item.description: A stalled cross-chain swap may still be processing or sending a refund. Check its inbound and outbound records before deciding whether to submit another swap.

item.title: Three Routes for Moving BTC Across Chains After RenBridge
item.description: BTC can cross chains through threshold-signed tBTC, custodian-issued WBTC, or exchange-wrapped cbBTC; each route trades reach and convenience for a different trust model.

item.title: Cross River Adds Ripple USD to Its Banking Platform
item.description: Cross River is adding Ripple USD on the XRP Ledger to its banking platform, giving fintechs one API for stablecoin settlement alongside ACH, wires and real-time payments.

item.title: Why Bridge Pools Pay Out Before Inventory Rebalances
item.description: A bridge can deliver destination tokens before source funds arrive; relayers, pool accounting and later rebalancing explain how inventory and risk move.

item.title: A Cross-Chain Swap Failed. What Should You Check Before Retrying?
item.description: A failed cross-chain swap can mean a reverted deposit, a delayed message or a failed payout; check the on-chain state before sending funds again.

item.title: Keep Native SOL Available for a Swap After Bridging
item.description: A bridged token does not pay Solana fees: keep native SOL for the fee payer, possible token-account creation and failed swap attempts.

item.title: Why Your Crypto Left One Chain but Hasn’t Arrived
item.description: A confirmed source transaction proves only that a bridge accepted the request; follow its message or fill record, then verify the destination transaction and token.

item.title: Ledger details CryptoBilis implant as MediaMarkt halts sales
item.description: Ledger says an implant in CryptoBilis-sold signers read recovery phrases from their screens and sent them over LTE, prompting MediaMarkt Saturn to pause sales.

item.title: Set Slippage by the Swap Legs in a Cross-Chain Route
item.description: Set slippage against the swap legs in a cross-chain route, then verify the destination minimum, bridge quote, fees and failure path before signing.

item.title: Solana schedules Alpenglow consensus switch for Oct. 21
item.description: Solana will activate Alpenglow in epoch 1064 on Oct. 21, replacing TowerBFT’s vote transactions with direct validator certificates and targeting 150ms finality.

item.title: Acrossbridge: How Cross-Chain Transfers and Swaps Work
item.description: Acrossbridge combines a source-chain transfer with destination delivery and, when needed, a token swap; the route depends on liquidity, verification and finality.
